Cloud GPU prices: RTX 4090, 5090 and H100 per hour (Oct 2026)

# Cloud GPU prices for AI images and video

 By Alexandre S. Updated 13 Nov 2026 Last checked 13 Nov 2026 What changed 

A cloud GPU is a graphics card in someone else’s data centre that you rent by the hour to run AI models. VRAM, the card’s own memory, decides which models fit.

Of nine GPU clouds in the table, Novita lists the lowest on-demand rate for an RTX 4090, at $0.33 an hour on 12 November 2026. That is one cent under Runpod’s Community Cloud at $0.34. Novita’s RTX 5090, at $0.56, is the lowest 5090 in the table.

Runpod’s Community Cloud H100 PCIe, at $1.99, is the lowest on-demand H100 by one cent. Novita’s spot H100, which it can reclaim after the first hour, is $1.70. Vast.ai’s cheapest verified hosts undercut every list price on the L40S, A100 and RTX PRO 6000. Its RTX PRO 6000 is $1.08 against Runpod’s $1.69. Vast.ai figures count its verified hosts only.

On our own Runpod account on 17 October 2026, one 1280 x 1280 FLUX 3 Klein image took about 28.5 seconds on a Secure Cloud RTX 4090. At that tier’s rate it costs $0.007 of GPU time an image.

## Why the same H100 costs three times more across clouds

The spread comes from who owns the machine and how long you commit. An on-demand H100 runs from $1.99 an hour on Runpod’s Community Cloud to $5.95 on Paperspace on demand.

 Runpod’s pod rates per hour for 24 and 32 GB cards, 13 November 2026 Runpod GPU Cloud pricing page, captured 13 November 2026 

Runpod’s Community Cloud and Vast.ai rent machines owned by third-party hosts. Runpod’s Choose a Pod docs rate Community Cloud reliability as “Variable”, and Runpod no longer accepts new Community hosts.

Vast.ai’s hosts set their own prices: its 39 verified RTX 4090 offers ran from $0.41 to a middle price of $0.67.

 Vast.ai’s pricing page on 24 October 2026: marketplace prices per hour, shown as a lowest offer and a median Vast.ai live GPU prices, captured 24 October 2026 

Commitment is the second lever. Paperspace shows an A100 at $1.15 an hour, and only on a three-year term. Lambda prices its A100 SXM 80 GB only in machines of eight cards, at $2.79 per card.

 Lambda’s instances pricing on 24 October 2026: price per GPU per hour on the 8-GPU tab Lambda instances pricing, captured 24 October 2026 

Serverless costs more per hour and less per month when requests are rare. Runpod’s flex worker bills from start to full stop and scales to zero between jobs (Runpod pricing). Modal bills each second a function runs, with no charge between requests: its H100 rate of $0.0011 a second is $3.95 an hour (Modal pricing).

## What one image or clip costs

Price per hour tells you little until you know how fast the card works. The useful figure is cost per output: the hourly price divided by the outputs you finish in an hour.

 RunPod vs Vast.ai ComfyUI Cost: 10, 50 & 100 Images HostingCompared with Natalie 

 A creator prices ComfyUI image runs of 10, 50 and 100 images on Runpod and Vast.ai Video: RunPod vs Vast.ai ComfyUI Cost: 10, 50 & 100 Images, HostingCompared with Natalie on YouTube, 15 September 2026. 

 The GPU picker on 24 October 2026: each card shows memory and price per hour; the ComfyUI template defaults to a 150 GB disk Runpod GPU picker with hourly prices and the ComfyUI template selected, captured 24 October 2026 

On our own Runpod account on 17 October 2026, an RTX 4090 on Secure Cloud made 12 FLUX 3 Klein images in 342 seconds. Each was 1280 x 1280 at 16 steps, about 28.5 seconds an image.

The table below applies that time to each 4090 rate. Every row assumes the 28.5 seconds measured on Secure Cloud.

Scroll sideways for all 3 columns

The settings change the bill more than the cloud does. The full FLUX 3 Klein model at 50 steps took about 4 minutes an image on the same pod, $0.06 each.

These figures are GPU time only. Starting the pod, loading the model and storage come on top. Our Runpod pricing breakdown adds those up.

For video, time one clip on your own pod and divide. Runpod’s own hosted Wan 2.2 makes a 5-second 720p clip for $0.30 (Runpod pricing). A rented 5090 at $1.39 beats that only if each clip takes under 13 minutes (1.39 divided by 0.30 is 4.63 clips an hour).

## Which GPU for which job

VRAM is the first filter. A model that does not fit spills into the computer’s main memory (offloading), which works but runs slower.

Memory each job needs, and the cards in the table that hold it Scroll sideways for all 3 columns

| Job | VRAM it needs | Cards that fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ad stills with FLUX or similar image models | Models of 6 to 17 GB, on our own Runpod account | RTX 4090 or 5090 |
| Wan 2.2 5B video | Fits 8 GB with ComfyUI’s offloading, per ComfyUI’s docs | Any card in the table; RTX 4090 cheapest |
| Large video models near 40 GB | More than a 5090’s 32 GB, on our own Runpod account | L40S, A100 or RTX PRO 6000 |

Scroll sideways for all 3 columns

A video model of about 40 GB overflows a 5090 and offloads. On our own account, that overflow is why a 96 GB card can cost less per clip despite its higher hourly price. Wan 2.2’s model card says its 5B version “can also run on consumer-grade graphics cards like 4090” (Hugging Face).

Step-by-step setups are in Wan 2.2 on Runpod with ComfyUI and ComfyUI on Runpod. Our Runpod hub gathers the rest.

## The model’s licence goes with every rental
